name: Google Shape;200;p7
text:
Leakage discipline
shift-then-roll
Every rolling window is shifted by one match, so a fixture never sees itself. Only prior matches feed a prediction, and the walk-forward splits enforce it.
Mutation-tested guard
CI flips shift(1) to shift(0) and fails the build if the leakage tests stay green. A guard that never fails on a broken build is no guard at all.
One feature code path
Training and serving run the same code, so there is no train/serve skew to reconcile.

name: Google Shape;389;p15
text:
The negative result is the deliverable, and it is well evidenced
No model beats the market in any aggregate fold, league or track comparison: six families across nine configurations, three tuned.
On four common folds, tuned CatBoost scores 0.9749 and Dixon-Coles 0.9908; both trail the market at 0.9675.
On the deployed 2025-26 holdout, CatBoost scores 0.9853 vs market 0.9784—a stable +0.0069 gap.
No value threshold yields a profit whose CI excludes zero, and CLV is negative throughout.
Interpretation: public pre-kickoff data improves a price-blind baseline but adds no reliable edge beyond the closing market.
What we delivered: a reproducible, leakage-proof, versioned, deployed and monitored pipeline that establishes a negative result credibly.

CLV caveat: value is flagged against closing-derived probability, so this is not a clean bet-at-open simulation.
Understat is scraped, with no documented API. Its schema already changed once mid-project.
Cut from scope: historical injury data (no free feed) and prediction markets as a historical training source.
